# Fungi

> *How do fungi differ from bacteria, and why does being eukaryotic make them harder to target?*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
This chapter will follow the layout of [*Gram-positive cocci*](gram-positive-cocci.qmd). The plan:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| The group in one sentence | Eukaryotic microbes that grow as yeasts, moulds, or switch between the two with temperature |
| Sorting key | Yeast, mould or dimorphic; ergosterol versus cholesterol; who gets infected (host factors) |
| Main organisms | *Candida albicans* (commensal turned opportunist), *Aspergillus* (inhaled spores), *Cryptococcus* (capsule) |
| Supporting organisms | Dermatophytes, *Histoplasma*, *Pneumocystis* |
| Later in the course | Skin, lung and opportunistic infections in the organ blocks; antifungal drugs in pharmacology |
